findings.text: follow-on: build_worklist here duplicates the public function name of build_worklist in imas_codex/standard_names/harmonize.py:308, in the same package, with an unrelated capability (family-drift grouping versus near-duplicate pairing). They live in different modules so no import collides, but a reader or dispatcher writing 'from imas_codex.standard_names import build_worklist' has two candidates and the name no longer identifies a capability; the near-duplicate builder should be named for what it returns.

follow-on: plan section 4 says the worklist excludes the section 5 vectors, and neither build_worklist nor the driver applies any such exclusion; the driver feeds the live embeddings straight through. The omission is defensible because section 5 already re-embedded those 38 names and embedding-census.log records a 2,528-name census with identical_vector_clusters=0, so no section 5 vector survives to exclude; but the code carries no guard that would keep them out if the wrong embeddings reappear, so it protects the criterion by circumstance rather than by construction.

follow-on: the assertion 'assert len(states) == 2' inside the decide_batch stub compares the count of pairs the test itself passed to judge_worklist against the length of the state list judge_worklist builds from those pairs, so both sides move together and it holds however badly the state is built; it is a stub-interface sanity check, not a guard on the production transformation. The verdict and segment_judgments assertions on the same test are independent and carry this change's durability.
